feed.title: AI Base: recently added topics
feed.subtitle: A free, structured knowledge base for learning AI.

entry.title: Fundamentals
entry.summary: Welcome to the start of the road.

entry.title: What Is AI
entry.summary: This district answers the first question: what is AI? The honest answer is that the word covers a family of ideas, and which systems count depends on how you define it.

entry.title: What Counts as AI
entry.summary: Artificial intelligence has no single agreed definition, so whether something "counts" depends on the question you ask.

entry.title: AI, ML, DL and Generative AI
entry.summary: AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI are nested ideas, like Russian dolls.

entry.title: Rules vs Learning
entry.summary: There are two ways to make a machine behave well: write the rules by hand, or show it examples and let it work the rules out. Hand-written rules are clear but brittle.

entry.title: Narrow, General and Super AI
entry.summary: Narrow AI does one job, or a small family of jobs, very well. General AI would handle a wide range of tasks the way a person can. Superintelligence would go far beyond human ability.

entry.title: A Short History of AI
entry.summary: AI's history is a pattern of big promises, real breakthroughs, disappointment and funding cuts, then a new approach and a new wave. The two long slumps are called AI winters.

entry.title: The Agent
entry.summary: Almost every AI system, however different it looks, has the same shape: it is an agent inside an environment. It senses what is happening, decides what to do to reach a goal, and acts, over and over.

entry.title: Agents and Environments
entry.summary: An agent is anything that perceives its surroundings through sensors and acts on them through actuators to pursue a goal. The surroundings it lives in are its environment.

entry.title: PDA Loop
entry.summary: The Perception → Decision → Action loop is the heartbeat of every intelligent system.

entry.title: Goals, Utility and Rationality
entry.summary: An agent needs a way to choose between options.

entry.title: State and Representation
entry.summary: The state is the agent's summary of the situation: everything it needs to know to choose a good action, and nothing more.

entry.title: Kinds of Environments
entry.summary: Some AI problems are easy and others are brutal, and much of the difference lies in the environment.

entry.title: Data and Models
entry.summary: Before an AI system can decide anything, it has to perceive, and for most modern systems perceiving means turning the world into data.

entry.title: Data as Raw Material
entry.summary: Data is recorded information about the world: measurements, text, images, sound, clicks, transactions.

entry.title: Features and Labels
entry.summary: Features are the measurable facts a model looks at, and a label is the answer it is asked to predict.

entry.title: A Model Is a Function
entry.summary: A model is a function: give it inputs and it returns a prediction.

entry.title: Training vs Inference
entry.summary: Training is when a model's parameters are adjusted using examples. Inference is when the finished, frozen model is used to make predictions on new inputs.

entry.title: Types of Tasks
entry.summary: Most AI problems fall into a few kinds: classify (pick a category), predict a number, group similar things without labels, generate new content, or choose actions over time.

entry.title: Classic AI
entry.summary: Before machine learning took over, AI meant searching, reasoning and planning with hand-built knowledge.

entry.title: Search
entry.summary: Search is how a machine finds a path or a plan by exploring possibilities systematically.

entry.title: Heuristics and A-star Search
entry.summary: A heuristic is an informed guess about how far you still are from the goal.

entry.title: Logic and Knowledge Representation
entry.summary: Classic AI stored what it knew as facts and rules, and used inference to work out new facts from them. Writing knowledge in a form a machine can reason with is called knowledge representation.

entry.title: Planning
entry.summary: Planning is finding a sequence of actions that turns the current situation into a goal.

entry.title: Expert Systems and Their Limits
entry.summary: An expert system captures the knowledge of human specialists as a set of if-then rules and applies them with an inference engine. In the 1980s they powered a commercial AI boom.

entry.title: Judging AI
entry.summary: Building an AI system is only half the job. The other half is judging it: how do you know it works, whether it will keep working on new cases, and where it is likely to fail?

entry.title: Measuring Performance
entry.summary: To judge an AI system you have to count its hits, misses and false alarms, not just its overall accuracy.

entry.title: Generalization
entry.summary: Generalization is a model's ability to do well on examples it has never seen. A model that merely memorises its training examples, noise and all, scores perfectly on them and poorly on anything new.

entry.title: Where AI Goes Wrong
entry.summary: AI systems fail in patterned ways: they learn from unrepresentative or biased data, they meet a world that has changed since training, they can be brittle to tiny changes, and they can be…

entry.title: Anatomy of an AI System
entry.summary: Every AI system, from a thermostat to a chatbot, can be described with the same seven parts: a goal, the data it uses, a model or rule, and a loop of perceive, decide, act, all judged by some…
